title: Conditional κ=0.0010188195926446377: grouped capacity entrances and fifteen enlargements
body:
This adds seven compatible entrance gauges and fifteen entrance-space enlargements to the frozen propagated208 construction. The resulting **conditional κ is `127352449080579709023951 / (125 × 10²⁴) ≈ 0.0010188195926446377`**.

The additive package is `research/e8-capacity-grouped-composition`. Its complex coarse bound is `1019858644613497908431 / 10²⁴`; the freshly replayed corrected signed-nine bit bound remains `255384852701747 / 250000000000000000`. The complex supplier binds. The exact gain over the frozen PR376 parent `92328da595bc688146c79ab8308f0d2012bb491e` is `680708658374343412199 / 10²⁷`, approximately **0.06685813%**. This is a reproducible refinement of this construction, not a highest-current-score claim; newer architecture reports are separate work.

### Construction and attribution

**eumemic's [PR421](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/421)**, with OpenAI Codex assistance, supplies the unchanged rank-two capacity constructor, retained-snapshot checks and chronological frame propagation. **Rohan Arun's [PR422](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/422)**, with OpenAI Codex assistance, supplies the compatible grouped rank-one selection, incorporating the PR414/420 work credited in its retained notice. On our frozen208 word, the five rank-one plans followed by two rank-two plans add gauges **766, 917, 627, 948, 672, 435 and 367** through **27 literal shears and six additional A-frame changes**. The resulting 215 intermediate is independently source-bound, with full raw and retained-snapshot columns checked against the literal entrance prefix.

**eumemic's [PR423](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/423)**, with OpenAI Codex assistance, supplies the unchanged entrance-enlargement constructor and the local checker's additional A/B frame-baseline controls. Updated PR422 supplies thirteen compatible enlargement plans: the native selection's incompatible nongauged 785 plan is explicitly rejected, then the remaining eleven plans and its 914/960 pair are used. **Chafik Boukhalfa's [PR424](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/424), assisted by Anthropic Claude**, supplies the gauge 838 enlargement. Only that witness is imported; its target 125 prefix and fusion claims are not used.

Our final fixed witness enlarges gauge 891 from rank one to rank five with basis `[256,195,32,16,15]`, using the same unchanged PR423 constructor. It was found by a bounded 121-subspace screen; the portable verifier runs no search. Across the fifteen enlargements, all scalar groups, their order, all 1021 raw columns and retained snapshots remain equal to the 215 intermediate. **Thirty-three A/B frame labels change**, and the final **215 gauges have entrance dimension 393**. The actual response contains **7017 entries and 7118 signed unit macros**.

The source chains remain separate:208→215→thirteen enlargements→gauge 838→gauge 891. No independently reported gains are added together. The parent retains the earlier PR411/416/418 donor-prefix and compiler work, PR409/410 promotions and enlargements, our commuting windows, and Chafik Boukhalfa's PR402 target 177/220 re-synthesis with Anthropic Claude assistance. Dugongue's PR401/404 normalization machinery, Jacob Sussman's checkers, and all original R781/R822, signed-bit, geometry, compiler, license and attribution notices remain intact.

### Complete finite evidence and source scope

The default reruns the frozen208 parent and every ancestor, then checks the final candidate with:

- Exact native reconstruction, fresh actual nongauged response, **215 independent helper tokens** through complete response/main/cleanup, all 1021 scalar columns, helper diagonals and private cleanup. The final native local checker rejects **46 frame controls**: 12 against the inherited original-A baseline, 33 against the 215 A/B baseline, and one actual entrance omission. Two positions occur in both baseline classes; these are not 46 distinct frame changes.
- **978 exact Gaussian phase pairs**, **56 boundary frames**, **28,672 address-column checks**, and fresh source-bound prior phases.
- Complete T64 bank emission, owner routes, independent decoding and invoice: **5855 banks and 2711 rank-one pads per stage**, **114,135 live / 114,926 physical slots**, **2,584,719 paid children**, rank mass **8,311,887**, deficit **19,968**, and **247,680 boundary adapters**. The full per-vertex coefficient is **5,930,820,880,626,519**.
- Both exact moment engines, adjacent exclusion, the corrected signed-nine **91-bit prefix** and coefficient **71,903,549,476,531**, fresh **12,360-matrix** dyadic geometry, eight charged continuations and all **47 strict outer inequalities**. `eta = beta = 10^-30`; the counted common outer `log2` threshold is `14 × 10³⁰`. The required row coefficient **15,451** remains below **20,161**.

The unchanged legacy fixed-sixths `gxcore` **rejects clean-X at register 208 and gauged-only dirt at 275**. Those rejections remain explicit. Separately, exact Fraction replay and the actual paid copy/clear/add/double/HALF/divide3 streams pass all 1021 independent columns in both orientations. There are **111,776 forward / 116,462 backward real primitive steps**, including **8482 HALF and 1445 divide3 operations per orientation**; prefix denominator LCM is **24**. Private streams return to zero and the complete primitive bill is charged. No unchanged gxcore or Lean-facing acceptance is claimed.

The derived runtime replaces only the native local checker with the exact PR423 leaf and checks its complete inventory independently; the copied 410 manifest is provenance only. Two narrow byte-recorded adapters retain the target 171 omission control and strict protected-block/fresh-response bank contract. The native 409 program bytes remain unchanged in a copied runtime whose CONFIG is replaced by exact native 422 T64 bytes. Its `expected_kappa` and `benchmark_kappa` labels are source provenance only; only replicas and the unchanged deficit parameter feed the retained bank code, and our final score is freshly recomputed.

All-size normalized-window lifts, arbitrary correlated-bank substitution, recursive compiler/chart realization, ordinary calls, common-grid precision, prime/setup/recovery, fixed tapes/restored rows, analytic interfaces and a common dominating stage-specific `C_full` remain conditional. Finite source-template evidence does not establish an unconditional multiplication theorem or a separately materialized all-size global instruction stream.

### Separate fixed-inventory padding certificate

The eight-file [higher-capacity215 padding appendix](https://github.com/applecrusher/integer-mult-bounds/blob/codex-e8-reuse-extension/research/e8-higher-capacity-padding-bound/PROOF.md) proves the exact minimum **`2711 × (73^α − 1)` for `0 < α ≤ 1/100`**, with width 73 and prescribed ranks/counts `(9,8,7,5,4)` / `(36224,9472,1536,1152,1600)`. It exhausts **4765** legal bank patterns, verifies a rational dual using integer powers, and checks equality for every supplied bank. Arbitrary splitting of padding is covered. This does not optimize the real-child inventory, local program, width, full invoice or global score. Both previously published padding certificates remain unchanged and apply to their own inventories.

```sh
python -B research/e8-capacity-grouped-composition/verify.py /absolute/path/to/new-output
python -B research/e8-higher-capacity-padding-bound/verify.py /absolute/path/to/new-padding.json
```

The new workflow runs the complete default on Python **3.12/3.13** with C++17/Boost and pinned Python dependencies, then runs all three published padding certificates and preserves receipts. The parent restores its complete **414 native files**. The new bounded carriers restore **eight exact PR421/422 source/config/notice leaves and twelve exact PR423/updated422/424 leaves**; these are limited closures, not full unchanged upstream package replays. The default rechecks all **17 frozen dependency inventories**. All **19 previously published trees**, including both older padding appendices, remain byte-identical.
